findings.reason: The protected source is already the canonical optimal bit-manipulation solution: cancel all pairs, isolate a bit on which the two singletons differ, and cancel pairs independently in the two partitions. Its names express the mathematical concepts directly and it satisfies the mandated linear-time, constant-space bound, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local and immutable Accepted native sources have identical total-XOR pass, least-significant-bit isolation, partition condition, group accumulators, second pass, and return order; only collection typing syntax and the required LeetCode class-method wrapper differ.

The legal 64/512/4,096-value tiers retain two far-separated singleton values and force both complete XOR passes. The current source passes at +0.00 relative exponent with a 1.00x largest runtime ratio; a correct implementation that counts each value across the full array passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.72 with a 13.85x ratio.

The Approach proves pair cancellation, singleton separation, and independent partition invariants, states the two-pass constant-state bound, and now explains zero and negative-integer behavior separately.

The hash-bound public Reference remains verified against the source structure, preserving all three factual examples, the first example's either-order explanation, the explicit linear-time/constant-space requirement, and all three constraints.
